non_blocking: Check output shows an internal path. The node --test head line is built from the replaced argv (critic.ts:663 sets process.execPath, critic.ts:1278 uses `c.argv.join(" ")`), so See what was checked reads '/opt/node22/bin/node --test test/main.test.js -> exit 0 ...'. On a person's PC it would be the bundled node.exe path under their user folder. The critic model receives the same line. Tries show 'ran node src/main.js'. Suggest printing the head with the original 'node' (design §5 rule 3).

After a Continue, the card's spend can disagree with the session line (the fixer flagged this too). The card says 'It spent <task total> of its budget of <raised budget>' (budgetStop.spentUsdMicro). The session line comes from executor.ts:1767 pauseSentence(..., result.costUsdMicro, ...), which is the run's own spend. On a first pause the two agree. On a second pause they differ, and the session line then reads as more room than is left. Passing task.actual_cost_usd_micro + result.costUsdMicro there would make the area's 'agrees with the session line' decision hold in every case.

parseHandoff still pauses some near-siblings of the live phrasing. A reason after a full stop is not read: '- Nothing is needed for the two criteria. Each listed page gives its address and was opened.' plus an observation still gives both lines as leftToDo, because REASON only takes [:;,(–—-]. A pre-existing case: '- No further work is required to meet the acceptance criteria.' is read as an item. Both pause finished work the same way live check 3 did, if the model words it that way. Worth a case for C2/OP-4 or live check 4.

A reason that names work without a NOT_NOTHING word now reads as nothing. Example: 'Nothing for the criteria, though the tests need a rewrite' gives leftToDo [], where before the line was an item. The task then goes to review with the line as data, which fits 'done work is reviewed', but 'though' could join NOT_NOTHING.

The status label says 'at' next to cards that say 'before'. The Tasks tab, Overview 'Next' and drawer still show the label 'Paused at its budget' (task-words.ts:318) beside the card's 'paused before its budget ran out'. It names no amount, so it is a smaller mismatch than the blocking one.

The specialist-limit wrap-up card does not say what was spent. Its body is 'It has no budget of its own: it may spend CHF b per run.' (request-words.ts:712), while the session line says 'it spent CHF X'. That is the most common case (a task with no budget of its own). Its title phrase, 'paused before the <specialist>'s limit per run ran out' (47 characters), is always cut in the 60-character notification title once a project name is added. The fixer reported the notification cut for long project names.

An old Node is reported as missing. A probe that fails because Node is older than 18 is reported as 'Node.js is not installed where the checks run' (the `missing` text), although it is installed. This only matters in images other than node:22.

Every script directly in test/, tests/ or __tests__/ is run as a test file. A helper that starts a server and never exits would hit the check timeout and block the accept. The same file selection already existed for the told line; now the files are executed.

The composed L3-research-4 tests read the drawer's evidence through verificationIn(review.evidence), the function GET /tasks/:id uses, not over HTTP. The acceptance allowed the composed engine, and my bench walk confirmed the drawer over the real daemon.
